metaDescription: Seven 6-inch rise threshold ramps in aluminum, foam and rubber, compared on run length, slope, capacity and install style so you can match a real doorway.
introParagraphs: Six inches is a tall threshold. It is more than a sill and closer to a full step, so the ramp has to be longer, sturdier and more carefully chosen than the little wedges sold for a quarter inch lip. The seven picks below cover modular aluminum, solid foam, soft EVA and rubber, each with a different slope and footprint.

Slope is the number to check first. On a 6 inch rise, a 36 inch run gives a slope of 1 in 6, a 28 inch run gives about 1 in 4.7, and a 15 inch run is closer to 1 in 2.5. The 1 in 12 ratio used for public ramps would need 72 inches of run, so any short ramp for a 6 inch rise is a compromise that asks for strength or a helper.

We evaluated these from product pages and stated dimensions. A threshold ramp is a home aid, not a code-compliant entrance, and an occupational therapist can advise on slope for a specific chair, scooter or walker.

products.name: Nuvium Adjustable Threshold Ramp 2.6 to 6 in
products.description:
The adjustable Nuvium is the only pick here that bends to the doorway instead of forcing the doorway to match it. Independent heightening screws and swivel feet let you set the height between 2.6 and 6 inches. The access surface is 22 by 36 inches, and the corrosion-resistant aluminum alloy is listed for 1100 lb, the highest rating in the group.

At a full 6 inch setting on a 36 inch surface the slope is about 1 in 6, which is gentler than the 28 inch modular Nuvium and far kinder than the rubber wedges. Adjustment is also a risk, because a wrongly set foot can leave the ramp rocking, so check that all four feet touch.

In ownership, it stores as a portable aluminum platform and suits a home with two or three different thresholds. Compared with the fixed Nuvium 6 inch, it asks for more setup but gives more fit. A person choosing it should confirm the rise first, then set the screws and test with a helper nearby.
products.bestFor: Homes with more than one threshold height who want to dial in the fit.
pros: Height adjusts from 2.6 to 6 inches
Lists 1100 lb, the highest rating here
36 inch surface gives about 1 in 6 at 6 inches
Corrosion-resistant aluminum alloy build
cons: Adjustment screws add setup steps each time
Uneven feet can leave it rocking if set poorly

products.name: Nuvium 6 in Threshold Ramp Modular Aluminum
products.description:
This Nuvium is a fixed 6 inch modular ramp that measures 28.2 by 34 by 6 inches. Interlocking aluminum panels slide into place along internal guide rails, and anti-slip strips on the surface add traction. High-visibility yellow edges mark the boundary of the ramp, which helps at dusk and for anyone with weaker eyesight.

The slope is the thing to respect. A 6 inch rise over 28.2 inches of run is about 1 in 4.7, steeper than the 1 in 6 you get from the adjustable Nuvium or the Kritkin foam wedge. That is workable for a strong helper pushing a manual chair but demanding for independent use.

Ownership is easy: panels slide together, you secure it at the threshold and it comes apart for storage. The yellow edges also help prevent stepping off the side. It sits between the fixed foam options and the adjustable Nuvium in flexibility, and fits a doorway where a width of 34 inches is available.
products.bestFor: Doorways with a fixed 6 inch rise and a helper to steady the push.
pros: Yellow edges make the ramp boundary obvious
Interlocking panels slide into place easily
Anti-slip strips on the surface for grip
34 inch width gives side clearance
cons: Slope of about 1 in 4.7 is steep to push
Fixed height gives no room to adapt

products.name: VEVOR Door Threshold Ramp 6 Inch Rise Aluminum
products.description:
The VEVOR 6 inch ramp is built from 2 mm aircraft-grade aluminum and rated for 800 lb. It is modular, with an oval insert connection that lets sections slide together without tools, and the anodized finish is meant to resist rust and wear. The deck has a slip-resistant surface.

The listing gives no run length in the text we reviewed, so you cannot compute slope without checking the product page. That matters a lot at 6 inches, because the shorter the run, the steeper the climb. It is also very similar to the DWALE model, with the same 800 lb rating and tool-free assembly.

Ownership follows the modular pattern: you assemble sections to the height you need, secure the top and take it apart for storage. Compared with the 1100 lb Nuvium adjustable, it offers less fine tuning, but the build quality claims are clear. It suits a household that wants a straightforward, rust-resistant aluminum ramp.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a tool-free aluminum ramp with a clear 800 lb rating.
pros: Lists an 800 lb capacity on the product page
Built from 2 mm anodized aluminum
Sections slide together with no tools
Slip-resistant surface on the deck panels
cons: Run length is missing from the listing text
Few features separate it from the DWALE

products.name: DWALE Door Threshold Ramp 6 Inch Rise
products.description:
The DWALE ramp is another modular aluminum design with a stated 800 lb capacity. It lists use with wheelchairs, scooters, electric vehicles and walkers, and its oval insert connection slides sections together and apart without tools. The anodized aluminum is described as lightweight and has an anti-slip surface.

As with the VEVOR, run length is not in the text we reviewed, which makes slope hard to judge. Anyone choosing it should look up the dimensions on the product page and calculate the slope against the 6 inch rise before ordering. A steep result means it is better suited to a helper-assisted push.

In ownership, tool-free assembly is handy for moving the ramp between a front and back door. It stores in sections, which helps in a small closet. Next to the Kritkin foam wedge, it is harder and more rigid, and next to the Nuvium modular it offers fewer visibility cues.
products.bestFor: Households that want a rigid aluminum ramp that comes apart for storage.

Slides together and apart without tools
Named for wheelchairs, scooters and walkers
Anodized aluminum with anti-slip surface
cons: No run length in the reviewed text
Fewer visibility edges than the Nuvium

products.name: Silver Spring High-Density Composite Threshold Ramp
products.description:
The Silver Spring ramp is made from hard expanded foam with a solid, high-density core and a tough waterproof coating. It is listed for wheelchairs, mobility scooters and walkers, supports up to 800 lb, and comes in rise options from 1 to 6 inches. That range lets a household match different doorways within one product line.

Foam is quieter and lighter than aluminum, and it does not clang under a wheel. The tradeoff is that a solid wedge cannot be adjusted or taken apart, so measure the rise before you buy. The listing does not give a run length in the text we reviewed, so verify the slope on the product page.

In ownership, it can be set in place without assembly and wiped down when wet. Because the wedge is one piece, storage takes more room than a modular ramp. Against the Kritkin EVA wedge, this one is denser and has a stated capacity, so it is the better match for heavier chairs.
products.bestFor: Heavier wheeled devices that need a fixed, quiet, no-assembly wedge.
pros: Solid high-density foam core, 800 lb listed
Waterproof coating wipes clean
Available in 1 to 6 inch rise options
Needs no assembly or tools before use
cons: Fixed shape cannot adjust to odd thresholds
Run length is not shown in the reviewed text

products.name: Kritkin EVA Foam Threshold Ramp 36 x 36 x 6 in
products.description:
The Kritkin wedge is 36 inches long, 36 inches wide and 6 inches tall, so a 6 inch rise is spread across a 36 inch run for a slope of about 1 in 6. That is gentler than the 28 inch modular Nuvium. The material is lightweight EVA foam, and the grooved surface is meant to add traction on a bathroom or entry floor.

Soft foam flexes under load and absorbs small impacts, which is kind to floors and quiet underfoot. It also means the wedge may compress over time, and the page does not state a weight capacity, which is a notable gap for a mobility product. Confirm the rating with the seller before using it with a heavy device.

In ownership, it is easy to move and reposition, and nothing needs assembling. The width of 36 inches gives generous clearance for a walker or chair. Compared with the Silver Spring, it is lighter and cheaper in concept but less clearly rated, so it suits lighter users and lighter devices.
products.bestFor: Lighter devices and walkers that need a wide, soft, gentle-slope wedge.
pros: 36 inch run gives about 1 in 6 at 6 inches
Lightweight EVA foam is easy to reposition
Wide 36 inch deck gives side clearance
Grooved top adds traction underfoot
cons: No weight capacity in the listing text
Foam can compress with long use

products.name: DNA Motoring 5.7 inch Rubber Curb Ramp
products.description:
The DNA Motoring 5.7 inch rubber ramp is the shortest and steepest in the group, at 38.6 inches wide and only 14.8 inches deep. The rubber is wear-resistant, the top pattern is anti-slip, and grooves on both sides drain rain and melt water. It is a curb-style ramp more than a doorway ramp, and the listing frames it around heavy-duty loading.

Over a 14.8 inch run the slope is roughly 1 in 2.6, which is too steep for most wheelchairs and many scooters. It suits wheeled carts, a hand truck or an outdoor curb where someone strong is pushing. It does not carry a stated rating for wheelchairs in the text we reviewed.

In ownership, a solid rubber wedge is heavy to move but stays put on a driveway or garage floor. Compared with the Nuvium adjustable at 36 inches of run, it covers a rise of almost the same height in less than half the length. Treat it as an outdoor curb helper, and pick one of the longer ramps for wheelchair use.
products.bestFor: Outdoor curbs and garage edges where a strong helper moves wheeled loads.
pros: Wide 38.6 inch rubber deck suits carts
Drainage grooves clear rain and melt water
Anti-slip pattern on the top surface
Rubber stays put on a driveway
cons: Slope of about 1 in 2.6 is very steep
Single fixed height with no trimming

buyingCriteria.criterion: Run length for a 6 inch rise
buyingCriteria.explanation: The longer the ramp, the gentler the climb, and a 6 inch rise is where this matters most. The Kritkin spreads 6 inches across 36 inches for about 1 in 6, the Nuvium modular uses 28.2 inches for about 1 in 4.7, and the DNA Motoring 5.7 inch rubber wedge uses 14.8 inches for roughly 1 in 2.6. A 1 in 12 slope would need 72 inches. If a listing gives no run length, as with the VEVOR and DWALE, find it before you buy.

A fixed wedge matches one rise exactly, while an adjustable plate fits several. The Nuvium adjustable covers 2.6 to 6 inches, and the Silver Spring offers 1 to 6 inch versions as separate products. Measure the precise rise including the sill, since an inch of error changes the slope. If you have several doors with different heights, adjustability saves you from buying multiples.

Aluminum is rigid and stores in sections, solid foam is quiet and needs no assembly, EVA foam is light and soft, and rubber is heavy and outdoor-hardy. The VEVOR uses 2 mm aircraft-grade aluminum, the Silver Spring a solid high-density foam core and the Kritkin flexible EVA. Pick the material that matches where the ramp lives and who will move it. Soft foam is easiest to shift but may compress over time.

The capacity must cover the user, the chair or scooter and anything carried. The Nuvium adjustable lists 1100 lb, while the VEVOR, DWALE and Silver Spring list 800 lb. The Kritkin lists no capacity in the text we reviewed, so confirm it before using a heavy device. Treat the rating as a maximum and leave margin.

Both matter at a threshold where feet and wheels meet a wet or dim floor. The Nuvium modular has yellow edges and anti-slip strips, the Kritkin has a grooved top, and the DNA wedge has drainage grooves. Visibility cues help people avoid stepping off the side. Look for textured surfaces and keep them clean.

A ramp that slides is a hazard. Modular aluminum such as the DWALE and VEVOR assembles without tools but must be secured at the threshold. Foam wedges sit by their own weight and grip, and rubber stays put better on rough floors. Check that the top edge meets the sill without a gap and that nothing rocks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Slope and run length
howWeEvaluated.description: We calculated slope from stated length and rise. The Kritkin and the adjustable Nuvium lead at about 1 in 6 on a 36 inch surface, the modular Nuvium follows at about 1 in 4.7 and the DNA wedge is steepest at roughly 1 in 2.6. Listings with no run length lost credit because the slope could not be confirmed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and build
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated ratings and construction. The Nuvium adjustable leads at 1100 lb, the VEVOR, DWALE and Silver Spring list 800 lb, and the Kritkin gives no rating. Materials were weighed for rigidity, weather resistance and weight.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how well each ramp adapts to real thresholds. The Nuvium adjustable spans 2.6 to 6 inches, the Silver Spring comes in a range of fixed heights and the modular aluminum ramps assemble to size. Fixed single-height wedges scored lower for adaptability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Traction and edges
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed surface textures and edge cues. The Nuvium modular has yellow edges and anti-slip strips, the Kritkin has grooves and the DNA wedge has anti-slip patterning and drainage channels. This is based on product specs and buyer feedback, not measured friction.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We assessed assembly, weight and how each ramp stores. Modular aluminum comes apart, foam wedges move in one piece, and the rubber wedge is heavy. We favored ramps that one person can place without tools.

faq.q: How long should a ramp for a 6 inch rise be?
faq.a: The common 1 in 12 rule would need 72 inches of run, which most doorways cannot fit. Home guidance often accepts a steeper slope for short rises, but steeper means harder pushing and more tipping risk. Choose the longest ramp that fits and have a helper on hand.

faq.q: Which pick has the gentlest slope?
faq.a: The Kritkin and the adjustable Nuvium both offer a 36 inch run, which gives about 1 in 6 over 6 inches. The modular Nuvium is about 1 in 4.7 and the DNA rubber wedge roughly 1 in 2.6. Listings for the VEVOR and DWALE give no run length in the text we reviewed.

faq.q: Is the rubber DNA Motoring ramp safe for a wheelchair?
faq.a: It is a curb-style rubber ramp with a very steep slope of about 1 in 2.6, and the listing does not rate it for wheelchairs. Use it for wheeled carts or loads pushed by a strong helper outdoors. For wheelchair use, pick a longer ramp.

faq.q: Do foam ramps compress over time?
faq.a: Dense foam like the Silver Spring is made with a solid core and waterproof coating, but soft EVA such as the Kritkin can compress with long, heavy use. Inspect it for dents or cracks. Replace any ramp that no longer holds its shape.

faq.q: Will modular aluminum slide on a smooth floor?
faq.a: It can if it is not secured. The DWALE and VEVOR assemble without tools, and the Nuvium has guide rails, but you still need to anchor or brace the top at the threshold. Test with a gentle push before relying on it.

faq.q: How do I measure the rise properly?
faq.a: Measure from the lower surface to the top of the sill at the exact landing point, including any mat or weather strip. An inch of error changes the slope noticeably. If you are between sizes, choose the longer ramp.

faq.q: Do I need a professional to advise me?
faq.a: It helps. An occupational therapist can match slope and device to the user. Listed capacities describe design intent, and individual users and chairs vary.
